spots.name: Iowa State Capitol

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Iowa State Capitol, commonly called the Iowa Statehouse, is in Iowa's capital city, Des Moines.

spots.name: 801 Grand

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 801 Grand High Rise Building is an office skyscraper in Des Moines, Iowa, United States, operated and managed by JLL Americas and owned by Principal Financial Group.

spots.name: Basilica of St. John

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of St. John is a Minor Basilica of the Catholic Church in the Drake neighborhood of Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It is also a parish church in the Diocese of Des Moines. The church building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of St. John (Des Moines, Iowa)

spots.name: St. Ambrose Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Ambrose Cathedral is a historic building located in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, in the United States. It serves as a parish church and as the seat of the Diocese of Des Moines in the Catholic Church. The cathedral, along with the adjoining rectory, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

spots.name: Theodore Roosevelt High School
spots.summary: Theodore Roosevelt High School, usually referred to simply as Roosevelt High School or TRHS, is a public secondary school located on the west side of Des Moines, Iowa.

spots.name: Pappajohn Sculpture Park

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The John and Mary Pappajohn Sculpture Park is a 4.4-acre (1.8 ha) park within Western Gateway Park in Des Moines, Iowa. It opened in 2009 with 24 sculptures, with four more acquired later.

spots.name: Ruan Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ruan Center is a skyscraper located at 666 Grand Avenue in Des Moines, Iowa, which was built by Ruan Transportation. The building was completed in 1975 and stands at a height of 459 ft (140 m), and was the tallest building in Iowa until the completion of 801 Grand in 1991.

spots.name: Des Moines City Hall
spots.summary: The Des Moines City Hall is a government building in Des Moines, Iowa, built in 1909 and 1910. It was individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places on November 10, 1977 as the Municipal Building, and became a contributing property in the Civic Center Historic District in 1988.

photo.author: The original uploader was Iowahwyman at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Iowa State Fairgrounds
spots.summary: The Iowa State Fairgrounds is located on the east side of Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It annually hosts the Iowa State Fair in late summer. The state fair was begun in Iowa in 1854 and the current fairgrounds were established in 1886.

spots.name: Abraham Lincoln High School
spots.summary: Abraham Lincoln High School, usually referred to simply as Lincoln High School or Lincoln, is a public secondary school located in Des Moines Southside, Des Moines, Iowa, United States.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Abraham Lincoln High School (Des Moines, Iowa)

photo.author: Original uploader was Teddythetank at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Des Moines Marriott Hotel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Des Moines Marriott Hotel is a skyscraper hotel located in Downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States. The building rises 33 floors and 365 feet (111 m) in height. It is currently the 3rd-tallest building in the city and the tallest hotel in Iowa. The structure was completed in 1981 and contains 417 guest rooms.

spots.name: Polk County Courthouse
spots.summary: The Polk County Courthouse located in Des Moines, Iowa, United States, was built in 1906. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979 as a part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.

spots.name: Masonic Temple of Des Moines
spots.summary: The Masonic Temple of Des Moines is a historic Beaux Arts style building located in Des Moines, Iowa. Constructed in 1913, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) in 1997.

spots.name: HUB Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The HUB Tower is a high-rise office building located in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States. The building rises 25 floors and 325 feet (99 m) in height. It is tied with the EMC Insurance Building for the title of the 6th-tallest building in the city.

spots.name: Financial Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Financial Center is a skyscraper building located in the downtown area of Des Moines, Iowa. It was completed in 1973 and stands at a height of 345 ft (105 m). It was the tallest building in the city and state until the completion of the Ruan Center in 1975, and is currently the fourth tallest.

spots.name: Liberty Building
spots.summary: The Liberty Building is a historic building in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It has been a downtown landmark since 1923. The Liberty Building is located at the southwest corner of 6th Avenue and Grand Avenue in the heart of downtown Des Moines.

spots.name: Cathedral Church of Saint Paul

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Paul's Episcopal Cathedral, is located in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It is the cathedral church of the Episcopal Diocese of Iowa. The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places as St. Paul's Episcopal Church.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral Church of Saint Paul (Des Moines, Iowa)

spots.name: Fish and Game Pavilion and Aquarium
spots.summary: The Fish and Game Pavilion and Aquarium is located in the Iowa State Fairgrounds in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. The structure was erected with financial support from the State of Iowa. It was designed by the Des Moines architectural firm of Proudfoot, Rawson & Souers.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Fish and Game Pavilion and Aquarium

spots.name: Scottish Rite Consistory Building
spots.summary: The Scottish Rite Consistory Building in Des Moines, Iowa was built during 1926–1927. It is a late date example of Neo-Classical style architecture, designed by Roland Harrison, a partner in the Des Moines architectural firm of Wetherell and Harrison.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Scottish Rite Consistory Building (Des Moines, Iowa)

spots.name: Old Downtown Des Moines Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Downtown Des Moines Library is a historic building in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States that was built in 1903. It was individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977, and became a contributing property in the Civic Center Historic District in 1988.

spots.name: Drake Stadium
spots.summary: Drake Stadium is a stadium on the campus of Drake University in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. Best known as the home of the Drake Relays, it also serves as the home field of the university's football team. It opened in 1925.

photo.author: U.S. Navy photo by James Woods

spots.name: Principal Park
spots.summary: Principal Park, formerly Sec Taylor Stadium, is a minor league baseball stadium in Des Moines, Iowa. It is the home field of the Iowa Cubs of the International League.

spots.name: Crane Building
spots.summary: The Crane Building, also known as C.E. Erickson Co., in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. Crane Company was a plumbing and heating supplier and manufacturer that had this six-story manufacturing facility built in 1916. It was designed by the Des Moines architectural firm of Sawyer and Watrous.

spots.name: East Des Moines Industrial Historic District
spots.summary: The East Des Moines Industrial Historic District is a nationally recognized historic district located in the East Village of Des Moines, Iowa, United States, directly east of the Downtown Des Moines area.
spots.wikipediaTitle: East Des Moines Industrial Historic District

spots.name: Homestead Building
spots.summary: The Homestead Building, also known as the Martin Hotel, is a historic building in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. Designed by the Des Moines architectural firm of Smith & Gage, it was built in two stages. The eastern one-third was completed in 1893 and the western two-thirds were completed in 1905.

spots.name: G.W. Jones Building
spots.summary: The G.W. Jones Building, also known as the Electric Farm Lighting Co. and the Laster Motor Company, is a historic building located in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It is significant for its association with the rise of the automobile industry in the city. George W.

spots.name: Youngerman Block
spots.summary: Youngerman Block is a three-story commercial building in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States, incorporating Italianate architecture with later alterations that introduced Art Deco detailing. Built in 1876, the Youngerman Block was designed by architect William Foster (1842–1909) for Conrad Youngerman.

spots.name: Walnut Tire and Battery Co.-Globe Publishing Company Building
spots.summary: The Walnut Tire and Battery Co. Globe Publishing Company Building is a historic building located on the west side of downtown Des Moines, Iowa, United States. The two-story brick commercial building features two mirror-image sections that were completed four years apart.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Walnut Tire and Battery Co.-Globe Publishing Company Building

spots.name: Walter M. Bartlett Double House
spots.summary: The Walter M. Bartlett Double House is a historic building located in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. Built in 1913, the two-story structure features balloon frame construction. The Neoclassical style building originally had a large portico on the main facade that has been covered over.

spots.name: State Historical Society of Iowa Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Exhibits include a venture into Iowa's past when glaciers pushed their way through and mammoths roamed the plains, state's frontier and prairie past where kid-friendly activities such as pushing a plow or carrying buckets with a shoulder yoke can be had. Fossil, Native American, wildlife, and Iowa U.S. Civil War flags on display. Cafe Baratta's inside.

photo.author: Gage Skidmore from Surprise, AZ, United States of America

spots.name: Big Grove Brewery
spots.summary: Big brewpub whose dining room was once the showroom of the largest Chevrolet dealer in Des Moines. They kept the big glass windows but replaced the shiny Impalas with a central bar serving the brewery's mostly ale-styles, sours, and seltzers. They do a line of IPAs that are variations on their "Eddy" brand. The best brews are their malty dark beers, when they're available: their coffee stout is lu

spots.name: Confluence Brewing Company

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Large microbrewery whose canned beers are carried in Hy-Vee stores throughout the area, as well as by many bars and restaurants. The brewery has a taproom that welcomes visitors to sample just about everything they brew, including rarer small batch styles and special bottlings of barrel aged beers. The brewery is known for its excellent quality control and its ability to brew both ales and the mor

spots.name: Drake Diner
spots.summary: Drake location is the original location. Favorites such as omelets, French toast, reubens, crinkle-cut fries, and bacon cheeseburgers and Drake's own "Bulldog burger" dominate the menu (all three Diner's feature the Maytag Burger, oozing with Iowa's own Maytag blue cheese). During nice weather, there's a screened-in patio available to sit. Shakes and malts are made with Des Moines's very own Ander

spots.name: Exile Brewing Company

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Brewpub and microbrewery in a historic warehouse, brews a wide range of both ale and lager styles. Casual bar with outdoor patio and a large indoor dining room for dinner. The best beers tend to be their German-style seasonal beers, including dark lagers, a nutty-sweet marzen style (Octoberfest), and similar beers. They also produce a line of hard seltzers. Live music Sunday afternoons starting at

spots.name: Iowa Tap Room
spots.summary: A "must visit" for drinkers who want to experience Iowa beer in one place since the bar features beers and ciders from every craft brewery in the state of Iowa (even from far-flung places like Dubuque). The center area of the bar is a formidable "turret of taps" with more than 100 draft brews available. The menu focuses on down-home country cooking with specialties like bread pork chops with big d

spots.name: Zanzibar's Coffee Adventure

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Features local art displayed around the coffee house. Great spot to sit and drink a cup or talk, study. Sit at the coffee bar or a table. Serves great breakfast. Sells their amazing beans as well so you can enjoy their coffee at home. Very friendly to all walks of life. Also provides catering services and can be reserved for private parties and meetings. You can also order their beans online or ov

spots.name: Zombie Burger

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A popular local burger joint with a humorous undead theme — the decor inside is rife with references to zombie flicks — and lots of creative burger and milkshake creations. The menu is full of intriguing options worth exploring but of particular note is "the Walking Ched," a beef patty atop fried mac and cheese with bacon. The fries and shakes are also excellent. A bar in the back serves draft bee

spots.name: The Royal Mile Bar and The Red Monk

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: This is the place to go on Court Avenue if you want a good urban setting and a multitude of imported draft and bottled beers to from which to choose--nearly 30 on tap and over 100 bottled brews. More than 85 varieties of Scotch whisky as well. Downstairs is the English pub, Royal Mile, while upstairs is the Belgian themed Red Monk, with a wide variety of Belgian imports, including Trappist ales.

spots.name: Chuck's Restaurant

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: If the number of years one's been in business is the standard way to rate, few in Des Moines could mess with Chuck's more than 50-year reign on the northside of Des Moines. Chuck's has proven if you take old classics, such as spaghetti and meatballs, meatloaf, and steak, and treat them with respect, you'll be in the neighborhood for a long time. Excellent pizza.

spots.name: Fong's Pizza (Downtown)

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The original location, founded on January 26th, 2009, in the former King Ying Low, Des Moines' oldest operating Chinese restaurant. Elements of King Ying Low's history and décor were kept and the current Fong's Pizza menu is inspired by a fusion of Asian, Italian, and Polynesian cooking styles paired with the tropical and fun flavors of a Tiki bar.

spots.name: Twisted Vine Brewery
spots.summary: The second incarnation of Twisted Vine is in a restored historic building in the East End. They brew about a dozen beers, both ales and lagers, and also have a full bar with mixed drinks and guest ciders. The tastiest brew is a hefty Belgian Triple. They also do a nice, malty porter and if you're lucky, they'll have their unusual white stout.

spots.name: Hessen Haus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you order a pint, the whole place will look at you and ask, "What's wrong?" so it's best to get a half-liter. Although they do serve the mass-produced American standbys the reason it's popular is for the more than 15 German beers they offer. Serve wine and a full array of cocktails and traditional German food, too.

spots.name: Tursi's Latin King

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the longest-standing restaurants in the area (since 1947), the Italian cuisine and beautiful restaurant setting will please anyone with a desire for a bit of originality. Very busy during the lunch hour, particularly when the state's legislative branch is in session. Small patio available. Full wine list.

spots.name: B and B Grocery, Meat and Deli

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Family-owned and -operated since 1922. In 2008, the readers of The Des Moines Register voted their Dad's Killer as the "Best Deli Sandwich" in the city and many subsequent "best of" awards by locals. The Food Network's "Outrageous Food" featured the Killossal Sandwich, a combo of four sandwiches, in May 2011.

spots.name: La Mie Bakery and Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: French-style bakery featuring all the goods you'd imagine, with quality omelets and coffee. High ceilings and modern setting make it a popular place to dine for all 3 meals rather than simply carry out fare. Outdoor patio on the back with a few tables. Can also find offerings at Downtown Farmer's Market.

spots.name: 801 Chophouse
spots.summary: Being atop the Principal Building, along with their class of wines, steaks and seafood, 801 has a reputation for the city's nicest restaurant. The fare is amongst the best downtown, with freshness and ingredients resembling the prime rib (rare, get it?) being their ticket to success.

spots.name: Waveland Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you're expecting a fancy diner, then you better get lost. This place is for the real Saturday morning crowd and a good place to recover from a hangover. If it was legal to light up a smoke, this is where you'd get no gruff from fellow patrons.

spots.name: Chicago Speakeasy

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Des Moines classic, the restaurant features a mobster theme. Excellent prime rib (the house specialty), served in several sizes, an extensive salad bar, and a number of seafood offerings. Large portions.

spots.name: Flying Mango

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Began as a catering business but when their uniquely smoked Cajun and Creole creations caught on, they soon started to get a bigger loyal following. Full wine list.

spots.name: Christopher's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A restaurant with a great reputation for serving up quality prime rib and Italian dishes for over 50 years. The restaurant is larger than it appears from outside.
